title: Finite obstruction to the fixed F_256 quotient-coupled AG port
research_direction: Algebraic-geometric evaluation codes and quotient-coupled extensions
construction_markdown: The supplied paper's Construction 4.1 fixes K=F_256, an RM(1,7) inner realization of length 128 and distance 64, and two repair blocks of total length 16,512. Its finite theorem assumes a genus-g curve with L+1 distinct F_256-rational points and integers a,L satisfying a+1-g >= 1 and 128L+16,512 <= 2^30; it certifies distance 64(L-a). The finite parameter system has no solution when this certificate is required to reach 535,822,336.
theorem_statement: No specialization satisfying the hypotheses of Construction 4.1 in the supplied quotient-coupled AG-code paper can satisfy its Theorem 4.2 certified-distance inequality 64(L-a) >= 535,822,336 at block length 2^30.
proof_markdown: Put D=535,822,336 and q_0=D/64=8,372,224. The source theorem's distance certificate requires L-a >= q_0, while its Riemann--Roch eligibility condition a+1-g >= 1 gives a >= g. Hence L >= q_0+g. The source construction chooses L+1 distinct points of a curve over F_256. Hasse--Weil therefore gives L+1 <= 257+32g, hence L <= 256+32g. Thus q_0+g <= 256+32g, so g >= ceil((q_0-256)/31)=270,064, and then L >= 8,642,288. But the exact source length condition yields L <= floor((2^30-16,512)/128)=8,388,479, a contradiction. Separately, the source's uniform theorem assumes delta<7/15, whereas active delta=511/1024 exceeds 7/15 by 497/15,360. This is a scoped failure of the paper's fixed F_256 finite certificate, not an impossibility claim for arbitrary quotient-coupled or AG constructions.

explicitness_audit: This is a deterministic integer-and-Hasse--Weil audit; it selects no curve, codeword, or random object.
Every inequality comes from a displayed hypothesis or conclusion of the supplied finite construction.
The conclusion is explicitly limited to certification by the supplied fixed F_256 architecture.
distance_audit: The tested certificate is exactly 64(L-a), the minimum-distance guarantee in the source's Theorem 4.2.
The contradiction occurs before a positive-dimension code can be certified, so no target-distance candidate survives this port.
obstructions: The paper's Theorem 6.2 cannot be invoked directly because its stated range delta<7/15 excludes the active delta=511/1024.

More strongly, its fixed F_256 Construction 4.1 cannot satisfy its own finite target-distance certificate at length 2^30: the rational-point/genus requirement forces L>=8,642,288, while its length budget forces L<=8,388,479.
This does not rule out a different quotient-coupled construction with a changed field, inner code, repair geometry, or a sharper distance proof.
next_tasks: Do not submit a leaderboard record from this architecture without a materially changed finite construction and a new proof certificate.
If revisiting quotient coupling, optimize a different alphabet/inner-code scaling before choosing a curve; changing only the modular level or divisor cannot evade the proved conflict.
Use the existing genus-zero affine-inner candidate as the current concrete AG baseline rather than this failed direct port.

discussion_posts.subject: The supplied F_256 quotient-coupled architecture cannot reach epsilon=2^-10
discussion_posts.body_markdown: For Construction 4.1, target distance forces L-a >= 8,372,224, and its Riemann--Roch eligibility forces a >= g, so L >= 8,372,224+g. Its L+1 rational points over F_256 imply L <= 256+32g. Hence g >= 270,064, so L >= 8,642,288, contradicting the exact length cap L <= 8,388,479. This is a finite obstruction to the paper's fixed architecture, not to quotient coupling in general.

discussion_posts.subject: The paper's uniform delta range already excludes the new target
discussion_posts.body_markdown: The supplied paper's Theorem 6.2 assumes 0<delta<7/15, while active delta=511/1024 has 511/1024-7/15=497/15,360>0. The finite obstruction is stronger: it fails even without the theorem's asymptotic argument.
